maya: Heads-up: EU ingest lag -> ~18h of late events surfaced, dashboards showing a big drop. Starting a targeted reprocess for the 2026-03-19 window. Kicking off replay job now. @alex @sam please watch quotas and throttles.

alex: How many partitions affected? Any consumer group still stuck?

sam: Looks like 6 partitions in eu-prod-ingest, consumer lag peaked ~300k. Root cause was a node OOM during the nightly deploy. We're going to run replay with dedupe=true and staging topic so upstream aggregates don't double-count.

jordan: Prefer we run with conservative parallelism to avoid bursting downstream quotas. Set concurrency=8 and target rate=2000 msg/s to start.

maya: Plan: run in 1h batches (windowed), dedupe on event id, write to staging topic then upsert aggregates. Rollback hook is ready if drift > 0.5%.

alex: Can you paste the exact replay command so infra can validate quotas and reserve backfill-capacity?

maya: ```bash
replayctl start --env=eu --from=2026-03-19T00:00Z --to=2026-03-19T18:00Z \
  --parallelism=8 --rate=2000 --dedupe-key=event_id --staging-topic=telemetry.replay.eustage
```

sam: Monitoring: watch dashboard telemetry/replay-rate, aggregate-diff, and replay-loss. Alert if replay-loss > 0.5% or aggregate-diff > 0.2%.

replay-bot: Job 4921 started by maya. Current shards: 8. ETA ~3h. Logs: https://logs.redwood/job/4921

liz: @maya If we hit quota we should fail over to the dedicated backfill pool. I'm bumping backfill-quota for the org to 2x for this run.

maya: Thanks @liz — I'll watch diffs and pause if drift spikes.

alex: One more ask: after replay finishes we need a fast sanity recompute for DAU and session counts across EU. Can we run a single-shard canary recompute first?

sam: Yes. I'll run a canary recompute on shard-1 once replay completes, validate counts, then promote to full recompute.

maya: :thumbsup: posting progress here.

replay-bot: Job 4921 progress: 15% processed, throughput 1.9k msg/s, errors 0.01%.

maya: Update: paused at 48% due to a small spike in aggregate-diff (0.6%). Investigating root cause.

alex: Logs show a late schema change for 'session_length' introduced by a downstream client. Should we do a schema normalization pass before continuing?

jordan: If the schema change affects aggregation keys, run normalization in staging topic and re-run the canary.

maya: OK. I'll patch the transformer to accept both variants and resume after normalization. New ETA ~2.5h.

replay-bot: Job 4921 resumed by maya.

maya: Finished full run. Final status: processed all windows, final aggregate-diff 0.04% (within threshold). Marking ticket REDWOOD-613 resolved. Thanks everyone who helped.
